label: Card
title: Card
summary: Use a Card to group one product, offer, or article on a panel, with an optional logo, a picture, and a few lines of text.
corePrinciple: One card, one idea: a name and one fact.

anatomy.title: A header, a picture, and the text
anatomy.description: A panel stacks three slots: header for a logo or a label, media for a picture, and the content you pass as children, usually Card.SupportText and Card.Title. Each slot shows only when you pass it.
blocks: header: a logo or a label in a row padded 12 px.
media: a picture across the full width at 154:116.
Card.SupportText: a 12 px line for a category or a fact.
Card.Title: the name in 16 px heavy type, up to 3 lines.
children: a column padded 12 px, 4 px between lines.
AppearanceBrand sets the fill; corners are 12 px.

configuration.title: Two variants, three slots, and a fill
configuration.description: variant default shows a picture when you pass media; slim never does. Pass header for a logo or a label, media for a picture, and children for the text, and leave out what you don’t need. AppearanceBrand sets the fill: with no modes the card is Neutral white, as Figma draws it. Semantic Intent System tints it with AppearanceSystem’s status colour. Card Container Plain removes the panel; Page type SubPage and context 8 Section add a grey border.

states.title: Static or pressable
states.description: Without onPress the card is static. With onPress the whole card is one button: give it an accessibilityLabel when the title isn’t its whole name, and don’t put buttons inside it. It dims a little on hover and more while pressed, and a thin dark outline shows its focus. disabled dims it to half, stops presses, and takes it out of the Tab order; without onPress it does nothing.

sizing.title: Your layout sets the width
sizing.description: The card fills a column’s width but hugs its content in a row, so give it a width there; Figma and Storybook draw it at 200 px. Height follows the content. The picture keeps 154:116 of the width, and mediaAspectRatio changes that. The header and the text are padded 12 px, with 4 px between slots and between lines; Gap M and L widen both, and Gap None removes them.
blocks: 14 px between slots, 18 px between lines.

content.title: A name and one fact
content.description: Make the title the product or offer name, and each support line one fact: a category, a price, a date, or a status. The header is a logo or a label, not a second title. Card.Title stops at three lines with an ellipsis; Card.SupportText never stops, so keep it short.

inContext.title: Offers on the Home screen
inContext.description: Two offers share a row, each card taking half of it. The cards use the package default, Neutral white. Each card’s onPress opens its offer: the screen does the navigation, and the card only reports the press.

sources.title: Use the public Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Card has two variants, Default and Slim, drawn white (AppearanceBrand Neutral) at 200 px with fixed heights; in code the card hugs its content and is white by default too. Figma’s header and media switches are the header and media props in code: pass them or leave them out (false also hides a slot). The card doesn’t read the app’s theme, so pass modes on the card or place it in a Coin stack. The published Storybook still shows the older generated page.
